html:
The constitution of the Empire of Japan, issued as a gift from the Meiji Emperor to his people in February 1889 and in force from 1890 to 1947. It was the first modern constitution in Asia.

Its main author, Itō Hirobumi, toured Europe to study constitutions and chose a model close to that of Prussia and the German Empire, which kept strong powers for the monarch.

  • The emperor was sovereign, "sacred and inviolable", and held supreme command of the army and navy.
  • A two-house Imperial Diet made laws and approved budgets. The lower house was elected, at first by only about one percent of the people, men who paid enough tax; the upper house held nobles and appointees.
  • Rights were granted, but "within the limits of law".

It let party government grow in the 1920s, but because the armed forces answered to the emperor, not the cabinet, the military could later steer the state toward war. After defeat in 1945 it was replaced by the Constitution of Japan.
sum: The constitution of the Empire of Japan, issued as a gift from the Meiji Emperor to his people in February 1889 and in force from 1890 to 1947. It was the first modern constitution in Asia.
